Best home battery backup systems for Texas (2026)

For Texas homeowners, I would prioritize whole-home backup capability, reliable air-conditioning support, battery capacity, and value for money.

Texas has some unique requirements: summer heat, high AC loads, occasional winter storms, and power outages that can last longer than a few hours.

My top choices are Tesla Powerwall 3, FranklinWH, Enphase IQ Battery, and EcoFlow. The best one depends on whether you're looking for whole-home backup, solar integration, or an affordable alternative to a generator.

Top 4 home battery systems
Shop
Best overall

1. Tesla Powerwall 3

13.5 kWh capacity · 11.5 kW output

Estimated installed: $13,000–$16,500

Excellent for new solar installations and high-power appliances. Two units are a strong starting point for many Texas whole-home backup designs.

Shop

2. FranklinWH aPower 2

15 kWh capacity · 10 kW output

Estimated installed: $15,000–$20,000

My favorite alternative for existing solar systems, large AC loads, and homes that may combine batteries with a standby generator.

Shop

3. Enphase IQ Battery 10C

10 kWh capacity · 7.08 kW output

Estimated installed: $13,000–$17,000

Best for homeowners with Enphase microinverters. Modular design and a 15-year limited warranty.

Shop

4. EcoFlow DELTA Pro Ultra X

Expandable battery storage · portable/modular architecture

Example retail kit: $7,899.00

A flexible choice for emergency backup without a conventional permanent battery installation, though whole-home integration can still require an electrician and additional equipment.

Installed prices are approximate U.S. planning ranges, not Texas-specific quotes. Hardware, controllers, permits, and electrical work affect final costs.

These are preliminary sizing ranges. A central AC system can consume much of a battery's energy during a hot Texas day. A 27 kWh system powering an average 3 kW load would last approximately 9 hours before accounting for losses and reserve capacity.

For multi-day outages, solar recharging or a generator can be more practical than simply adding batteries.

Texas-specific incentives and considerations

Texas has some battery programs worth checking before purchasing. For example, eligible Tesla Electric customers can receive virtual power plant bill credits, while certain utility territories offer other battery incentives.

Best home battery backup systems for Texas (2026)

For Texas homeowners, my top picks are Tesla Powerwall 3, FranklinWH aPower 2, and Enphase IQ Battery 5P.

Texas has some unique considerations: summer air-conditioning loads, severe storms, occasional extended grid outages, and electricity plans that may reward storing energy when prices are low.

The best battery depends on whether you want to power your entire house, keep essential appliances running during an outage, or reduce your electricity bills.

Top 3 home batteries compared

Best overall

13.5 kWh capacity | 11.5 kW output

Estimated installed price: $13,000–$16,500

Great for new solar installations and homes with high electrical loads. Strong output for running air conditioning, subject to proper sizing.

2. FranklinWH aPower 2

Best for whole-home backup

15 kWh capacity | 10 kW output

Estimated installed price: $15,000–$20,000

Excellent for extended outages, existing solar systems and generator integration. Offers a 15-year limited warranty.

These are planning ranges, not guarantees. For example, a 27 kWh battery system supplying an average 2 kW load lasts roughly 12 hours after allowing for some losses. Solar can extend that runtime if the system supports charging during outages.

My recommendation for Texas

For a typical 2,000–3,000 sq. ft. Texas home with central air conditioning, I would start by comparing two Tesla Powerwall 3 units (27 kWh) against two FranklinWH aPower 2 units (30 kWh).

Also ask installers about storm preparation, air-conditioner startup current, backup transfer equipment, and whether your electricity plan supports time-of-use savings.
